title: GLP-1 picks and shovels: the fill-finish and delivery-device capacity beneath the molecule
map_limitation: Five blind spots specific to THIS map. (1) The equipment layer that gates the ramp is mostly unlisted, so supplier-side EDGAR full-text search cannot reach it: Syntegon, OPTIMA, groninger, Bausch and Stroebel and IMA Group are private or have been taken private, and the largest dedicated sterile fillers are the same story, with Catalent sitting inside Novo Holdings and Vetter, Fareva, Recipharm and PCI Pharma Services all private. aseptic-filling-and-isolator-equipment therefore carries three listed names against an order book whose two largest owners publish nothing, and sterile-fill-finish-capacity carries five against a stage the originators largely perform in house. That is a finding about the chain, not a gap in the search. (2) The device platform layer is private in the same way: SHL Medical, Nemera, Owen Mumford and Phillips-Medisize file nothing, so the ticker list on autoinjector-and-pen-platforms is what is left after four of the layer's principals are removed. (3) Most listed names here file outside the SEC and reach this map through research rather than through full-text search: 1SXP.DE, GXI.DE, DAE.SW, YPSN.SW, SKAN.SW, KRN.DE, GETI-B.ST, MIKN.SW, BANB.SW, PPGN.SW, LONN.SW, SFZN.SW, AV.MI, SDZ.SW, NOVO-B.CO, 5214.T, 8086.T, 600529.SS, 0386.HK, 2359.HK, 207940.KS, RELIANCE.NS, SUNPHARMA.NS, CIPLA.NS, BIOCON.NS and PPLPHARMA.NS. Only GLW, XOM, WST, ATR, BDX, STVN, TMO, ATS and RDY are reachable that way, and STVN and RDY are foreign private issuers filing 6-K and 20-F rather than 10-Q, so the quarterly cadence the screen assumes does not exist for them. (4) Three quantities this thesis rests on are directionally sourced and quantitatively soft. Nobody discloses GLP-1 filling line utilisation, so capacity constrained for multiple years rests on one quantified lead time that belongs to a different stage (18 to 36 months for large-scale peptide synthesis capacity) and one qualitative statement (sterile lines take several years to design, validate and qualify). Nobody splits GLP-1 revenue by container format, so the syringe versus cartridge versus pen question the signal actually asks cannot be answered from any disclosure on this map; West's 18% of net sales and Stevanato's high value mix are the closest available and neither is broken out by format. And the qualification lock-in that makes a second supplier take years is asserted by every trade source opened this run and quantified by none: the nearest thing to a measurement is Datwyler beginning GLP-1 component supply in 2026 for a medicine launched years earlier. (5) The map cannot see substitution away from itself. The oral Wegovy tablet launched on 5 January 2026 and passed two million prescriptions in a quarter. A dose that ships as a tablet consumes no glass barrel, no plunger, no filling line and no pen, and no source opened this run sizes how much injectable volume it takes. That is the single largest risk to every link from position 4 to position 11, and it is recorded here rather than scored, because scoring it is the heat stage's job.

links.name: Type I borosilicate glass tubing
links.role: The raw input beneath every glass vial, cartridge and syringe barrel on this chain: a short list of tubing drawers melt and draw pharmaceutical grade Type I borosilicate tube, which converters then reform into containers, so tubing output sets the physical ceiling on container supply long before any filling line is involved.

evidence.claim: Demand from monoclonal antibodies, GLP-1 drugs and mRNA vaccines is driving unprecedented volume requirements for the Type I borosilicate glass that vials and syringes are made from.
evidence.source_name: Mordor Intelligence, Pharma Glass Tubing Market
source_excerpt: A wave of monoclonal antibodies, GLP-1 drugs, and mRNA vaccines is driving unprecedented volume requirements for Type I borosilicate vials and syringes.

evidence.claim: Nipro Corporation allocated USD 398 million (EUR 366 million) to a North Carolina plant slated to add 2 billion vials annually from late-2025, which is tubing capacity being turned into finished containers at scale.
evidence.source_name: Mordor Intelligence, Pharma Glass Tubing Market
source_excerpt: USD 398 million (EUR 366 million) to a North Carolina plant slated to add 2 billion vials annually from late-2025.

bottleneck.note: ARCH-004. Type I borosilicate is not substitutable inside an approved container closure system, and the melt-and-draw asset base is small and slow, but tube itself is a global traded good with no local logistics rent, which is why this is HIGH and not CHOKE_POINT. The largest drawer, SCHOTT AG, is foundation owned and unlisted.

capture_inputs.supply_concentration: The tubing market is repeatedly described around the same five names (SCHOTT AG, Corning, Nipro, Nippon Electric Glass, Gerresheimer). Two of the five are unlisted or foundation owned, so the listed slice understates concentration.
capture_inputs.substitutability: Within glass, none: a container closure system is approved against a glass type. Away from glass, cyclic olefin polymer barrels exist and are a real route around this link, which is why the criticality stops at HIGH.
capture_inputs.logistics_constraint: Tube is shipped globally and is not a regional pricing-power asset, unlike the cement link on tibet-mega-dam where hauling cost created the rent.
capture_inputs.who_posted_the_margin: Not resolvable from any source opened this run. Tubing sits inside larger groups at every listed name here, and none of them break it out, so the margin question passes to the heat stage as PENDING rather than as a fact.

links.name: Halobutyl rubber feedstock
links.role: The polymer the sealing surface is made from: bromobutyl and chlorobutyl rubber, produced by a handful of integrated petrochemical groups that sit entirely outside pharma, compounded downstream into the stoppers, plungers and seals that touch every injected dose.

evidence.claim: Bromobutyl rubber is the material of choice for stoppers in vials, syringes and cartridges because of its low extractables, high impermeability and compatibility with a wide range of drug formulations.
evidence.source_name: IndexBox, Halobutyl Rubber Market Forecast Points Higher Toward 2035
source_excerpt: Bromobutyl rubber is the material of choice for stoppers in vials, syringes, and cartridges due to its low extractables, high impermeability, and compatibility with a wide range of drug formulations.

evidence.claim: The halobutyl rubber market that feeds pharmaceutical closures is projected to grow at a compound annual growth rate of approximately 4.2% through 2035, with the market index reaching 145 against a 2025 base of 100.
evidence.source_name: IndexBox, Halobutyl Rubber Market Forecast Points Higher Toward 2035
source_excerpt: The market is projected to grow at a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of approximately 4.2% through 2035, with the market index reaching 145 (2025=100).

bottleneck.note: ARCH-004 with the opposite answer to the magnet link on humanoid-actuators. The material is genuinely critical to the dose but the producers are petrochemical majors for whom pharma grade butyl is a rounding error, so no listed name here is a way to own this chain. Recorded for completeness, and named as a trap: buying XOM is not buying GLP-1 capacity.

capture_inputs.supply_concentration: Concentrated in a few integrated petrochemical producers, with ExxonMobil and Arlanxeo repeatedly named as the global leaders and Sinopec, Reliance and JSR as regional players.
capture_inputs.substitutability: For the elastomer function inside an approved closure, none in practice: the closure is qualified as a formulation. For the supplier's own economics, complete, because the same plants serve tyre inner liners.
capture_inputs.who_posted_the_margin: Not the pharma chain. The pharmaceutical stopper application is a small share of halobutyl consumption, so the margin recorded downstream at elastomer-closure-components is not being taken here.

links.name: US Section 232 tariffs and onshoring agreements
links.role: The policy shock that re-sites this chain rather than growing it: a 2026 proclamation puts a headline 100% tariff on patented pharmaceutical imports with a lower rate for companies that sign onshoring agreements, which turns where a barrel is converted, a dose is filled and a pen is assembled into a tariff decision, and pulls capacity toward US sites on a 2026 to 2030 clock.

evidence.claim: On April 2, 2026 the President issued a Proclamation invoking Section 232 of the Trade Expansion Act of 1962, and beginning July 31, 2026 a 100% tariff applies to pharmaceutical articles that are subject to a valid, unexpired U.S. patent, with a +20% rate instead for companies operating under an approved onshoring plan until April 2, 2030.
evidence.source_name: Crowell & Moring, Trump Administration Imposes Section 232 Tariffs on Patented Pharmaceutical Imports
source_excerpt: On April 2, 2026, President Trump issued a Proclamation invoking Section 232 of the Trade Expansion Act of 1962
Beginning July 31, 2026, a 100% tariff will apply
Pharmaceutical articles that are subject to a valid, unexpired U.S. patent
Active pharmaceutical ingredients ('APIs') and key starting materials
+20% percent rate, in addition to the general applicable rate, until April 2, 2030

evidence.claim: Manufacturers have pledged a combined total of more than $480 billion in US-based production over the next four to ten years, and collectively those announcements point to 22 new manufacturing sites and roughly 44,000 new jobs, which is the demand signal the sterile filling stage is being asked to absorb.
evidence.source_name: Pharmaceutical Commerce, FAQ: Where US Pharma Reshoring Stands in 2026
source_excerpt: have pledged a combined total of more than $480 billion in US-based production over the next four to ten years.
Collectively, those announcements point to 22 new manufacturing sites and roughly 44,000 new jobs.

evidence.claim: The suppliers upstream of those pledged sites, the ones that would build the device and assembly capacity, were only cautiously optimistic about the demand as of the third quarter of 2025, and share prices across the sector had largely not moved to reflect the scale of the pledges.

evidence.claim: BD announced a $110 million investment to expand its production of prefillable syringes, of which $100 million establishes BD Neopak Glass Prefillable Syringe production at its Columbus site, with supply expected to begin in mid-2026, framed explicitly as strengthening its American manufacturing footprint as demand for biologics and GLP-1s accelerates.

bottleneck.note: ARCH-006, wired in as an extra topological root the way global-hydro-spillover was on tibet-mega-dam. There is no instrument for a tariff schedule, so example_tickers is deliberately empty; the investable expression of this link is the US-sited capacity at positions 4, 9 and 11, which is why all three carry an edge from here.

capture_inputs.supply_concentration: Not applicable: this is a policy, not a supplier. What it concentrates is location, by making non-US conversion and filling of a patented product carry a headline 100% tariff.
capture_inputs.substitutability: The stated route around it is an onshoring agreement, which substitutes a +20% rate for the headline rate until April 2, 2030, and an MFN pricing agreement which removes the additional tariff. Both are negotiated, not bought.
capture_inputs.who_posted_the_margin: Unknown and worth doubting. The only source opened this run that asked the question found equipment suppliers cautiously optimistic and their share prices largely unmoved, which argues the pledged dollars have not yet turned into orders.

links.name: Vial, cartridge and syringe barrel converters
links.role: The stage that reforms tube into the actual container a GLP-1 dose sits in, and where the format war is decided: prefillable glass syringes, sterile cartridges for pens, and specialty vials each need their own converted lines and their own customer qualification, so a format shift is a multi-year capital decision rather than a product choice.

evidence.claim: SCHOTT Pharma reported a revenue increase in Q1 2026 of 4.8% at constant currencies to EUR 240.2 million, with continued strong demand for sterile cartridges and specialty vials, and continued to invest in the expansion of its capacities in the first quarter of 2026 with the focus on sites in Switzerland and Hungary.
evidence.source_name: SCHOTT Pharma, media release: SCHOTT Pharma with positive start to financial year 2026; outlook confirmed
source_excerpt: Revenue increase in Q1 2026 by 4.8% at constant currencies to EUR 240.2 million.
continued strong demand for sterile cartridges and specialty vials
continued to invest in the expansion of its capacities in the first quarter of 2026, particularly for HVS. The focus was on sites in Switzerland and Hungary

evidence.claim: Gerresheimer is building a new production facility at its site in Wertheim, Germany for ready-to-fill and ready-to-use vials, a 4,000 m2 production hall slated to be completed by mid-2027, while SCHOTT Pharma inaugurated new capacity for core and specialty vials at its site in Lebanon, Pennsylvania with an investment of more than $60 million.

evidence.claim: The formats these converters make are what strains the filling stage: demand for prefilled syringes, autoinjectors and patient-focused delivery systems, particularly for GLP-1 therapies, is intensifying that strain, and prefilled syringes are becoming the preferred delivery format for high-value biologics.

evidence.claim: A converter's container is designed into the device it will be sold in: a Stevanato Group customer received regulatory approval in several European countries for a liraglutide-based therapy that incorporates the company's Alina pen injector platform, a project that embeds its cartridge technology into that pen platform.
evidence.source_name: Stevanato Group, press release: Stevanato Group Delivers 8% Revenue Growth for the Second Quarter of Fiscal 2026
source_excerpt: A customer recently received regulatory approval in several European countries for a liraglutide-based therapy that incorporates Stevanato Group's Alina® pen injector platform.
This important customer project also embeds our world-class cartridge technology into the Alina® pen platform, harnessing the power of our integrated capabilities.

bottleneck.note: ARCH-001. Converted line capacity, not glass availability, is what gates container output, and every listed name here is spending on it at once (SCHOTT Pharma in Switzerland and Hungary, Gerresheimer at Wertheim, BD at Columbus). Simultaneous expansion by everyone is the classic setup for the scarcity rent ending; that is a heat-stage question, recorded here as a fact and not scored.

capture_inputs.supply_concentration: Four listed converters (Stevanato, SCHOTT Pharma, Gerresheimer, BD) plus Nipro and Chinese capacity carry most of the named expansions; the same four names recur in every source opened this run.
capture_inputs.substitutability: Low at the drug level and high at the chain level. A filed product cannot change container supplier without requalification, but a NEW programme can be placed with any of the four, which is why capacity is being added by all of them at once.
capture_inputs.logistics_constraint: Qualification, not freight. The constraint that creates pricing power here is the customer's regulatory lock to a specific supplier's part, not the cost of moving glass.
capture_inputs.who_posted_the_margin: SCHOTT Pharma's own Q1 print shows the mix effect (high value solutions carrying growth while overall revenue grew 4.8% at constant currencies), which is the first place on this chain where the GLP-1 mix is visible in a reported number.
capture_inputs.shared_bill_of_materials: BDX also appears at autoinjector-and-pen-platforms and STVN at three links on this map. One bill of materials wearing several tickers is a single bet; noted here so the screen does not count it twice.

links.name: Stoppers, plungers, seals and coatings
links.role: Every dose has a rubber part touching it: the plunger in a syringe, the septum in a cartridge, the stopper on a vial, plus the fluoropolymer or spray coating that keeps the drug off the rubber. This is the most concentrated component layer on the chain and the one where GLP-1 revenue is already visible as a reported number in two listed issuers.

evidence.claim: GLP-1 therapies accounted for 18% of West Pharmaceutical's net sales, with GLP-1 elastomer revenues contributing 10% and GLP-1 West Vantage revenues adding 8%, while High Value Product Components net sales reached $409.3 million, up 29.6% on a reported basis.

evidence.claim: Demand increased for spray-coated plungers particularly suited to biologics, prefilled syringes and homecare applications, which are the parts inserted into a syringe at the filling stage rather than at the converter.

bottleneck.note: The qualification lock lives here. A drug is approved against a named supplier's component, and Datwyler's own release shows what a second source looks like in practice: supply of components for one GLP-1 medication STARTING in 2026, years after that medication was launched. Three listed names, so not thin coverage, but the concentration is real.

capture_inputs.supply_concentration: Two names carry the disclosed GLP-1 revenue on this map. West reports GLP-1 at 18% of net sales with the elastomer half at 10%; Datwyler discloses its first GLP-1 component supply starting from one US site.
capture_inputs.substitutability: The lowest on the chain. Component change on a filed product means requalification, which is why a second supplier arrives years late rather than at the next order.
capture_inputs.logistics_constraint: Regulatory rather than physical. The site is named in the filing, so US-sited capacity (Middletown, Dublin serving global) is not interchangeable with any other plant without a change filing.
capture_inputs.who_posted_the_margin: This link, visibly: West's High Value Product Components net sales of $409.3 million grew 29.6% on a reported basis, the largest disclosed growth number anywhere on this map.

links.name: Ready-to-use sterile containment
links.role: The stage that moves washing, siliconisation, crimping and sterilisation off the drug maker's floor and onto the converter's, sold as nested pre-sterilised syringes, cartridges and vials. It is a quiet transfer of value from the filler to the component supplier, and it is where the GLP-1 container volume is going.

evidence.claim: SCHOTT Pharma's 1.5 ml sterile cartridge is the smallest sterile format to date in its cartriQ portfolio and is critical for the stable storage of insulin, GLP-1 drugs or hormone therapies.
evidence.source_name: Manufacturing Chemist, SCHOTT Pharma expands ready-to-use portfolio with sterile 1.5 ml cartridge
source_excerpt: The 1.5 ml sterile cartridge represents a significant expansion of SCHOTT Pharma's cartriQ portfolio and offers the smallest sterile format to date
critical for the stable storage of insulin, GLP-1 drugs, or hormone therapies

evidence.claim: The ready-to-fill and ready-to-use vial market is expected to grow at a compound annual growth rate of around 13% until 2030, against an estimated $400 million in disclosed investments industry-wide for capacity additions in devices supporting GLP-1s.

source_excerpt: is expected to grow at a compound annual growth rate of around 13% until 2030
estimated $400 million in disclosed investments industry-wide for capacity additions in devices supporting GLP-1s

evidence.claim: For ready-to-use products the converter handles the washing, siliconisation, crimping and sterilisation processes from pharmaceutical manufacturers, so the container reaches the filling line already sterile and the filler's own preparation suite is bypassed.
evidence.source_name: Manufacturing Chemist, SCHOTT Pharma expands ready-to-use portfolio with sterile 1.5 ml cartridge
source_excerpt: For our RTU products, we handle washing, siliconisation, crimping, and sterilisation processes from pharmaceutical manufacturers.

bottleneck.note: The most under-described link on this map and the one the signal's own thesis names first. It is not a different product from position 4, it is a different SPLIT of the work, and the split is what moves margin. Same tickers as position 4 plus West, which is exactly why the screen must not count them twice.

capture_inputs.supply_concentration: The same four converters, since ready-to-use is a capability bolted onto their own lines rather than a separate industry.
capture_inputs.substitutability: A filler can route around this link by keeping its own washing and sterilisation suite, which is the honest limit on how much pricing power ready-to-use carries. What it cannot do is switch ready-to-use supplier on a filed product.
capture_inputs.who_posted_the_margin: Not separable from position 4 in any disclosure opened this run. Every converter reports ready-to-use inside a high value solutions or high value products aggregate, so this link's margin cannot be isolated from a filing and is recorded as unresolved.

links.name: Aseptic filling lines, isolators and barrier systems
links.role: The machine layer: high-speed syringe and cartridge filling lines and the isolators and barrier systems that make them compliant, ordered years before they run and installed on multi-year projects, which is why this link and not the molecule sets how fast GLP-1 supply can physically grow.

bottleneck.note: ARCH-001 in its purest form on this chain, and ARCH-003 inverted: the two largest filling-line OEMs, Syntegon and OPTIMA, are private, and IMA was taken private, so most of this order book publishes nothing. What is listed is the isolator and barrier half (SKAN) plus two diversified machine builders. SKAN's own backlog running into 2028 is the closest thing on this map to a dated lead-time figure.

capture_inputs.supply_concentration: Named repeatedly as Krones, Syntegon, IMA Group, OPTIMA and KHS, with Krones alone above 16.2% share in 2025. Three of the five are private or inside private ownership.
capture_inputs.substitutability: None inside a project once a line is specified, and the switching cost is the requalification of the filled product, not the machine price.
capture_inputs.logistics_constraint: Installation and qualification time. SKAN's disclosed order intake carries projects with durations extending into 2028, so an order placed now is capacity that arrives after the window this signal is written for.
capture_inputs.who_posted_the_margin: SKAN posted the growth (order intake up 16.3%, backlog up 27.8%, net sales up 22.2%). Whether the two private OEMs posted more cannot be established from any source opened this run, which is the central coverage hole in this link.

capture_inputs.who_posted_the_margin: Not resolvable this run. The USD 1.5 billion 2025 pool is an outsourced-market sizing, not a margin disclosure, and the originators do a large share in house, which no source opened this run sizes.

links.name: Sterile fill-finish capacity
links.role: Where the peptide, the container, the closure and the machine finally meet: the aseptic filling operation itself, split between the originators' own plants and a contract layer, and the single stage every GLP-1 label expansion has to queue for because designing, validating and qualifying a sterile line takes years.

evidence.claim: Designing, validating and qualifying sterile lines requires several years, limiting the speed at which supply can adjust, and global revenue for the fill-finish manufacturing market is estimated at US$11 billion in 2025 and projected to grow at a CAGR of 10.1 percent between 2025 and 2035.
evidence.source_name: Visiongain, Fill-Finish Manufacturing Is Now a Strategic Constraint

Global revenue for the fill-finish manufacturing market is estimated at US$11 billion in 2025 and is projected to grow at a CAGR of 10.1 percent between 2025 and 2035.

evidence.claim: Biologics, biosimilars and GLP-1s drive demand for sterile injectable drug products, and PCI Pharma Services announced in May the addition of sterile fill/finish and drug-device delivery combination capabilities to U.S. sites as part of a $1 billion global expansion program.

bottleneck.note: ARCH-001 and ARCH-003 at once. It is the convergence node of this map, taking six upstream edges, and it is also the least investable of the constrained links because the biggest dedicated fillers are private or captive: Catalent sits inside Novo Holdings after the 2024 transaction, Vetter, Fareva, Recipharm and PCI Pharma Services are private, and the originators fill much of their own volume.

It is a separate capital line and a separate order book from the filling line, and it is the one link on this map whose GLP-1 order flow has already visibly turned.

The equipment IS the gating step for device output, and yet the one listed pure-ish player that discloses the segment reported life sciences revenue down 9.3% and total backlog down against the prior year, while describing new bookings as being OUTSIDE autoinjector GLP-1 assembly equipment. capture_inputs.who_posted_the_margin: ATS is the only issuer on this map that breaks out a segment close to this link, and what it posted was a decline: life sciences revenue down $38.9 million or 9.3% year over year with backlog at $1,958 million against $2,139 million.

bottleneck.note: ARCH-003 in its investable form. It is the order book every link above sells into, and unlike the Yajiang developer or the frontier labs it is fully listed and fully crowded, so it is the schedule and never the trade. It is also the link that can delete demand for positions 4 through 11 without any of them doing anything wrong, by shifting the dose to a tablet.

capture_inputs.supply_concentration: Two issuers set essentially the whole order book, and both are integrating backwards into the very stages this map is about: Lilly's Pennsylvania site is explicitly an injectable medicine AND DEVICE facility.
capture_inputs.substitutability: The suppliers are substitutable to the anchor over a programme's life; the anchor is not substitutable to the suppliers at all. That asymmetry is the reason to hold the map and not the anchor.

notes.text: THE THESIS WAS TESTED AND IT SURVIVES WITH TWO CORRECTIONS AND ONE WARNING. The signal names six unmapped layers: sterile fill-finish lines, ready-to-use vials and cartridges, autoinjector and pen assembly, elastomer stoppers and glass barrels, single-use bioprocessing consumables, and the qualification bottleneck. Five of the six are on this map as their own links and every one of them cites a dated source fetched this run. CORRECTION 1: the qualification bottleneck is not a stage, it is a property, and it could not be cited as a stage. Nothing found this run describes a qualification and validation SERVICES layer with its own dated economics; what the sources describe is qualification as the switching cost inside positions 4, 5, 7 and 9. It is therefore recorded in each of those links' capture_inputs and bottleneck notes rather than built as a link, and the map says so instead of padding. CORRECTION 2: single-use bioprocessing consumables could not be cited AT ALL for this chain. The only Sartorius material reachable this run was undated product pages, and no dated source opened this run ties sterile filtration or single-use assembly demand to GLP-1 fill-finish specifically. A stage I cannot cite is not a stage, so it was dropped and named here rather than carried on the map with a decorative citation. THE WARNING, and the most important thing this build found: the capacity story and the order books already disagree in two places. ATS, the one listed issuer that discloses a segment close to pen and autoinjector assembly equipment, reported life sciences revenue down $38.9 million or 9.3% year over year, total backlog down to $1,958 million from $2,139 million, and described its new life sciences bookings as being OUTSIDE autoinjector GLP-1 assembly equipment. And the only source opened this run that asked whether the $480 billion of pledged US reshoring had reached upstream equipment suppliers found them merely cautiously optimistic with sector share prices largely unmoved. Meanwhile the demand anchor's fastest-growing product is a tablet that needs none of this chain. A heat run that scores this map as a pure shortage story without pricing those three facts is scoring the press releases, not the chain. STAGES CHECKED AND NOT BUILT, with the reason each: single-use consumables and sterile filtration (no dated GLP-1-specific source, above); contract sterilisation services for ready-to-use formats (could not be separated from the converters' own in-house sterilisation by any dated source, so it is folded into ready-to-use-containment-formats, whose own citation states the converter performs washing, siliconisation, crimping and sterilisation); cold chain and 2 to 8 degree distribution (real, and no dated source found this run connects it to GLP-1 device volumes rather than to pharma logistics generally); needle and cannula supply (not researched to a dated source in the time available, and named here so the next pass knows it is missing, not absent); secondary packaging, labelling and serialisation (folded into device-assembly-automation, whose equipment sources cover inspection and packaging in the same order book); and cyclic olefin polymer resin as its own raw-material link (the polymer route is real and is named in the glass tubing link's substitutability, but every COP source reachable this run was an undated product page, so the feedstock link was narrowed to halobutyl rubber, which could be cited). ARCHETYPES: ARCH-001 applied three times (primary-containment-converters, aseptic-filling-and-isolator-equipment, device-assembly-automation) and it is the spine of this chain; ARCH-004 applied twice (pharma-glass-tubing HIGH, halobutyl-elastomer-feedstock MEDIUM, the same shape landing at two different criticalities exactly as the archetype predicts); ARCH-003 applied twice, once inverted at aseptic-filling-and-isolator-equipment where the order book owners are private, and once in its investable form at glp1-demand-anchor; ARCH-006 applied once at us-onshoring-tariff-response, wired in as an extra topological root, which is the fourth chain in the corpus to carry it and the second where it changed the map rather than decorating it. ARCH-002 checked and did NOT fire: there is no EPC or competitively bid civil layer on this chain, because the buildings are the customers' own. ARCH-005 checked and did NOT fire: no power or grid equipment layer is material here. ARCH-007 checked and did NOT fire: no semiconductor layer is material to a glass, rubber and spring chain, and the connected-device electronics that would carry one are a feature, not a stage. NO CONFLICT WITH THE ARCHETYPE LIBRARY was found on this build, so nothing is escalated.
